items.notes: Route table names the identity/views page and its question; no answer on identifiers or avoiding a graph service.
Storage-selection route names document-access trade-offs; no embedding or record-lifecycle reasoning.
Defines failure classes and recovery-point validity; nothing on regaining authority after failover.
Reservation boundary register frames lifecycle unknowns, not business success versus notification.
Four-axis table separates deployment boundary from domain and data-ownership/state-authority axes.
States authentication alone does not authorize object access; explicit object policy required.
Ledger cites propagation and outbox sources; no explanation of local record versus external effect.
Separates HTTP method semantics from business-effect deduplication; no expired-key test guidance.
WAL and replication sources only; base-backup/PITR artifact list absent.

Names hedging among amplifiers of offered work; section is about GC pauses, not hedged-read design.
States a closed-loop generator can hide external demand, so load appears manageable.
CPU-bound pool-replacement regression; no permit, capacity or admission reasoning.
Tasks are not business demand and more tasks add no database connection capacity; admission stays separate.
Carrier starvation under pinning; a different failure mode from DB-permit admission.
Requires explicit edge semantics, direction and traversal limits before interpreting a path.
Cites bounded variable-length traversal and explosion concerns; no bounding technique.
Semantic data-equality proof dimensions aimed at migration state, not consumer contracts.
Route names SLI/objective pages; no statement of the indicator-versus-objective difference.
Chapter index lists SLI/SLO coverage only; no distinction between indicator and objective.
Mission statement names compatibility windows and irreversibility; no evidence gates listed.
Averages conceal bursts and hot-key pressure; no uniform-key test mechanism.
Same route-level claim that averages conceal hot-key pressure; no test design.
Exchangeable APIs preserve hidden semantic incompatibility; the word must be translated, not just the interface.
Defines L=lambda*W over mean residence time and notes tail drivers; no substitution argument.
Contrasts trace-correlation identity and durability with an authoritative audit record.
Notes tracing gives correlation not durable business truth, inside a workflow-selection topic.
Span existence is not commit proof; sampling or absence implications are not stated.
Stock-flow fundamentals route; no offered-work accounting per integration step.
Route asks which inputs must be explicit before comparing candidates; no input list.
Replay hashes lock model and scenario and detect drift; not aligned inputs for fair comparison.
Points to evidence layers and label vocabulary; no evidence requirement for measured inputs.
Records achieved error and fixed replication count for reproducibility; no result-hash rationale.
Enumerates run-record fields and a hash over substantive fields; no rationale for including limits.
Lists run records as metrics, convergence, hashes and limits; no explanation of the hash.
Unstable tie-breaking: equal-time events depend on hash order.
Model-family selection and resolution; no retry or timeout behavior.
Result table shows capacity and timeout effects; disciplines and controls are not enumerated.
Simulation-based provisioning assumes the future input distribution; drift invalidates more sampling.
Volume scope limits (uncalibrated inputs, no production claims); no replication-versus-distribution argument.
Describes a quadratic screen and its limits; no comparison with full Sobol analysis.
Names the quadratic response-surface screen in engine scope; no Sobol comparison.
Reports relative-error thresholds and convergence status; no near-zero mean caveat.
States the 0.02 relative-error gate; no near-zero denominator caveat.
Statistical-validity gate covers convergence and sample size, not converged-but-unsupported decisions.
Procedure separates declared input distributions from output CI; no calibration argument.
CIs are normal approximations across replications and calibration is uncalibrated for every model.
Lists hard, soft and non-quantitative constraint declarations; no failure-treatment comparison.
